text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Inventories at the ARO SA car manufacturer in Cimpulung Muscel are on the rise, the paper says.
- Rivers in western Romania have reached flooding levels.
ADEVARUL
- The National Liberal Party asked the government to cut taxes on profit.
- Sorin Dimitriu, the head of the State Ownership Fund (FPS), asked the Interior Ministry to support FPS in its demarches to withraw the funds deposited with the private Columna Bank.
- Japanese businessmen are interested to invest in Romania's Romtelecom telephone operator and in the nuclear power plant at Cernavoda.
- Shall Gas Romania will invest four million dollars to build a gas terminal in the county of Satu Mare.
General:
ADEVARUL
- Romania will have one million inhabitans less in 2017 following a low birth rate.
- Gypsy gangs in Bucharest ask shopowners to pay "protection fees".
ROMANIA LIBERA (g)

- Romania will use all possibilities offered by the Partnership for Peace programme to boost its chances to be admitted in the second wave of NATO's enlargement, Defence Minister Victor Babiuc is quoted as saying.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Some 20,000 Romanians are infected with the HIV virus and likely to develop it into full AIDS, the paper says.
- The Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR) asked authorities to take legal steps against nationalists who painted Romania's flag on bilingual signs in the city of Tirgu Mures.
- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
